references.text: The men of Gilead gathered earlier under Jephthah to fight against the Ammonites, which shows Jephthah's role as leader of Gilead.
Jephthah was chosen as leader and chief over Gilead, which explains his authority to gather the men of Gilead.
Jephthah and the men of Gilead fought together against the Ammonites and won, showing their military experience together.
The men of Ephraim also complained about not being called to battle under Gideon, a similar pattern of conflict between Ephraim and other tribes.
Gilead was part of the tribe of Manasseh, which explains the connection between Gilead, Ephraim, and Manasseh mentioned in the verse.
Gilead was given to Machir, son of Manasseh, showing the geographical and tribal relationship between Gilead and Manasseh.
